openwrt_wiki.installing_on_v5:
{{:media:tplink:tp-link_tl-wa801nd-v5_pcb.jpg?600|TP-Link TL-WA801ND v5 PCB}}

Pre-built images are available starting with release 19.07.

Don't try to update the firmware from the web interface, it'll brick your device. Anyway, to install it (or unbrick):

  * rename the bin/.../xxx_recovery.bin to **tp_recovery.bin**
  * put it in your tftp folder
  * the router expects TFTP at **192.168.0.66**
  * power device on with reset button pressed until the rightmost led is lit (the lock) to enter TFTP recovery mode

Once it's installed, do a normal sysupgrade with the squashfs image you built, also found in bin dir of the sources

openwrt_git.betreff: ramips: add support for TL-WA801ND v5
openwrt_git.text: Specification: System-On-Chip: MediaTek MT7628NN; CPU/Speed: 580 MHz; Flash-Chip: ELM Technology GD25Q64; Flash size: 8192 KiB; RAM: 64 MiB; Wireless No1: SoC-integrated: MT7628N 2.4GHz 802.11bgn. Currently the only method to install openwrt for the first time is via TFTP recovery. After first install you can use regular updates. Flash instructions: 1) To flash the recovery image, start a TFTP server with IP address 192.168.0.66 and serve the recovery image named tp_recovery.bin. 2) Connect your device to the LAN port, then press the WPS and Reset button and power it up. Keep pressing the WPS/Reset button for 10 seconds or until the lock LED is lighting up. It will try to download the recovery image and flash it. It can take up to 2-3 minutes to finish. When it reaches 100%, the router will reboot itself.

beitraege.text: Hello there. I tried to detect UART pinout for TP-Link TL-WA801ND rev5 accordingly to documentation from openwrt and one more wonderful article This is what I measured so far: grnd for sure is detected via multimeter’s continuity. TxD seems correct as well since voltage jumps around during boot TP_Link_TL-WA801NDv5_serial_uart_pinout1920×2557 362 KB What conclusion should I make? Is some resistor missing?

I flashed such a device over the serial port years ago. It was around so I opened it. Indeed, the voltage between RX and GND is 0 V, but serial works fine. The weird thing is that I couldn't get it to work with putty and had to use Tera Term. Just solder a connector and go ahead.
